title: Anticyclotomic Euler system over biquadratic fields: the ring-class exact sequence
author: Kim Tuan Do
work: Anticyclotomic Euler system over biquadratic fields
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Proposition (source0.tex lines 797--817, source label ringclass): for a prime that does not divide six times the class number of the real quadratic subfield and a squarefree ideal of the biquadratic field of suitable norm, the p-part of the ray class group of the biquadratic field modulo that ideal fits into an exact sequence whose outer terms are the two partial ray class groups attached to the two quadratic subfields, with the map described by an explicit reciprocity identification, and the projection followed by the reciprocity map is described on elements by a Frobenius element; delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 819--837 (one adjacent proof environment of 19 lines that opens and closes inside the retained span). The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span together with the retained context display. It writes the exact diagram of unit groups and ray classes for the three fields involved, takes p-parts, uses the assumption that p does not divide six times the class number and the structure of the unit groups of the quadratic subfields to identify the two horizontal outer terms, derives the first exact sequence from the middle arrow together with the retained decomposition display, and then identifies the Frobenius element describing the second part by comparing the primes of the two quadratic subfields lying above the given split prime. The proposition is a structural step in the construction of the article's anticyclotomic Euler system over biquadratic fields, where it controls the norm-compatible classes modulo an ideal. H2: a research-level algebraic-number-theory proposition whose proof combines class field theory exact sequences, p-part and unit-group analysis, Artin reciprocity identifications and a Frobenius comparison; it is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
